rules: Stop re-deriving the close/low/high range-position formula (stochastic-style position of close within a rolling high/low range) by only changing the window length or swapping one price field; two variants of this family were rejected this round for near-duplicate correlation and shared archive structure.

Small edits to an already-archived formula, one operand or one window changed, still overlap heavily in structure and get caught as a near-duplicate; when reusing a family that's already in the archive, change the functional form (e.g. normalize by dispersion instead of range) rather than tweaking a single parameter.

In ratio-style factors (return sum scaled by volatility), keep numerator and denominator on the same lookback window; a short-over-long mismatch (3-day sum over 21-day std) failed the cheap screen far worse than a matched long-over-long version (126-day over 126-day) that got accepted.

Multiplying two independently-ranked short-horizon sub-factors (a short return-sum rank times a volatility-ratio rank) nearly cancelled out to zero signal this round; treat that combination pattern as low-probability unless each sub-factor already shows signal on its own.

Lookback windows approaching 200 days are cutting it close on coverage for this universe and period; the longest window accepted this round was 126 days, so anything beyond that needs an explicit coverage check before proposing.

Piecewise return transforms (clipping to positive-only, or taking absolute value) combined into a ratio at a 21-day window landed just under the cheap-window bar; this shape needs a different window or a simpler transform before resubmitting.
Standalone timing-of-extremum features (where in a long window the min or max occurred) showed almost no signal alone this round; don't resubmit these without pairing them with a stronger co-factor.

The strongest results this round normalized a price or range value by dispersion measured over that same single window rather than mixing two separate windows; favor this self-normalization pattern for price_volume niches over multi-window combinations.

prompt:
You are keeping a short working memory for a factor search on US large-cap
equities, fitted on 2000 to 2013.

Below is what happened in the round just finished on this island: which
proposals were accepted into the archive with their fitness, and which were
rejected with the reason. Fitness is a t-statistic of the mean daily rank IC,
scaled by year-to-year stability and charged for complexity and turnover.

ACCEPTED
  fitness   1.970  niche fast/price_volume/high  -SIGN(TS_DELTA($close, 2)) * CS_RANK($volume / (TS_MEAN($volume, 15) + 1e-8))
  fitness   2.381  niche fast/price_volume/low  CS_RANK(($close - TS_MIN($close, 15)) / (TS_STD($close, 15) + 1e-8))
  fitness   0.840  niche fast/price_volume/low  CS_RANK(COUNT($return > 0, 21))
  fitness   1.300  niche fast/price_volume/low  CS_RANK(TS_SUM($return, 126) / (TS_STD($return, 126) + 1e-8))
  fitness   1.611  niche slow/price_volume/high  CS_RANK(($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($high - $low, 21) + 1e-8))

REJECTED
  -CS_RANK(TS_SUM($return, 3) / (TS_STD($return, 21) + 1e-8))
      cheap_screen: |t| 0.21 < 1.00 on the cheap window
  CS_RANK(TS_MEAN(MAX($return, 0), 21) / (TS_MEAN(ABS($return), 21) + 1e-8))
      cheap_screen: |t| 0.83 < 1.00 on the cheap window
  CS_RANK(TS_ARGMIN($close, 42) - TS_ARGMAX($close, 42))
      cheap_screen: |t| 0.31 < 1.00 on the cheap window
  SIGN($close - TS_MEAN($close, 200)) * CS_RANK($volume / (TS_MEAN($volume, 10) + 1e-8))
      coverage: 0.899 < 0.90
  -CS_RANK(TS_SUM($return, 5)) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 10) / (TS_STD($return, 63) + 1e-8))
      cheap_screen: |t| 0.03 < 1.00 on the cheap window
  ($close - TS_MIN($low, 19)) / (TS_MAX($high, 19) - TS_MIN($low, 19) + 1e-8)
      correlation: |rho| 0.995 >= 0.80 against `($close - TS_MIN($low, 21)) / (TS_MAX($high, 21) - TS_MIN($low, 21) + `
  ($close - TS_MIN($low, 21)) / (TS_MAX($close, 21) - TS_MIN($low, 21) + 1e-8)
      archive_subtree: shares 5 nodes with `($close - TS_MIN($low, 21)) / (TS_MAX($high, 21) - TS_MIN($low, 21) + `

Write at most 8 short rules that would make the next round better.
A useful rule is specific and actionable: "correlations between price and volume
over windows under 5 days were rejected for low coverage" beats "prefer robust
factors". Do not restate the hard limits, which are already enforced. Do not
propose expressions here.
